chapter_title_en: Letter of Tariel to the Khatavians
chapter_expert_explanation_en: Tariel dispatches ambassadors to King Ramaz of Khataeti demanding his personal attendance and tribute to India.

stanzas.english_translation: "I sent a man to Khatavet’hi and a letter from me; I wrote: 'The king of the Indians is of a truth powerful from God; every hungry soul of those faithful to him is sated; whosoever is disobedient will have himself to blame (for any ill that may befall him).
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 14 ('Letter of Tariel to the Khatavians', Stanza 387; Wardrop Stanza 373): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel dispatches ambassadors to King Ramaz of Khataeti demanding his personal attendance and tribute to India.

stanzas.english_translation: "'Brother and lord, by you we will not be embittered. When you see this command wend hither; if you come not we shall come; we will not steal upon you. It is better you should come to us, spill not your own blood.'
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 14 ('Letter of Tariel to the Khatavians', Stanza 388; Wardrop Stanza 374): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel dispatches ambassadors to King Ramaz of Khataeti demanding his personal attendance and tribute to India.

stanzas.english_translation: "I sent the man, I gave my heart up yet more to rejoicing, I made merry at court; the fire unbearable in its burning was extinguished. Then the world, Fate, gave me lavishly what I desired; now I am mad, so that I annoy even the wild beats if I approach them.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 14 ('Letter of Tariel to the Khatavians', Stanza 389; Wardrop Stanza 375): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel dispatches ambassadors to King Ramaz of Khataeti demanding his personal attendance and tribute to India.

stanzas.english_translation: "At first the plan of roaming, then reason soothed me. I feasted with my comrades, but the greatness of desires hindered me from joy; sometimes they filled me with melancholy, I uttered curses against Fate.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 14 ('Letter of Tariel to the Khatavians', Stanza 390; Wardrop Stanza 376): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel dispatches ambassadors to King Ramaz of Khataeti demanding his personal attendance and tribute to India.

act_title: Act II: Tariel's Chronicle of India, Love & Loss

location.desc: Tributary realm of King Ramaz, subdued by Tariel in his heroic campaign.

key_maxim_en: Better a glorious death than a shameful life!
